ios.desc:
iCanText – A Bigger, Smarter Keyboard That Moves With You

iCanText is a custom iOS keyboard built to make typing easier, clearer, and more comfortable. Featuring large, easy-to-tap keys, a gentle swaying animation, and smart visual cues, iCanText helps you type with more speed and fewer mistakes. 

Features:

* Oversized Keys for Confident Typing.

* Designed for accuracy and comfort.  iCanText gives your fingers more space.

* The top row gently moves left and right that allows for a maximum overall key size.

* Next-Letter (instead of next word) predictions.

* Likely next-letters glow based on what you're typing, making it faster to spot and tap what comes next.

* Natural gesture-based texting: swipe right for a space, left for a backspace, up for numbers, down for symbols, and keep swiping up for phrases and dialects. Double swipe down toggles caps.

* Single tap contractions. One tap makes a 'll, 's, 'r, 't, 'm or 've.

* Tap the "Fix it" key (the wrench) to correct typos, caps, and formatting.

* No pressure from autocorrect.

* Just type. You can fix your typos later.

* Custom keyboard styling (colors, etc.) in the main app.

* No Ads, No Tracking, No Distractions.

* iOS 26 users: have Apple's on-device LLM fix your typos.

Whether you're a fast typer, someone with larger fingers, or just want a more relaxing keyboard experience, iCanText will help you text better.

quotes.story_title: iPhone Typos? It's Not Just You – The iOS Keyboard Is Broken [video]

quotes.text:
== The problem ==

I’ve never been able to text properly on a phone.  I’ve tried with two thumbs, one thumb, and every other way I can think of. Nothing works for me. I can only seem to text with my right index finger while holding the phone in my left hand, which is at best is slow and full of typos.   I find myself fighting autocorrect as much as using it.  I tried swipe keyboards (gboard, etc.) but they didn't help.  Sometimes I watch people texting rapidly with both thumbs and marvel at their dexterity.  It's all very frustrating for me.

== A solution ==

So I set out to build a custom iPhone keyboard designed around one idea: making the keys as large as possible.

Initially, I wanted to build a transparent keyboard that would overlay the whole screen, but iOS doesn't allow this.  So I made as much room for larger keys in the allowed keyboard real estate by:

* Removing frequently used keys (spacebar, backspace and shift), and replacing them with gestures

* Removing keys for accessing focused keyboards (numbers, symbols, and saved phrases), also replacing them with gestures

* Nixing Autocorrect (which never helped me much) to recoup the room it takes.

Wth this maximal room, I set off to render the largest keys of a QWERTY keyboard that I could.  I found that the maximum key size is constrained by the middle row of the QWERTY layout.
